newsitem.title: CHILE: Codelco hopes to wrap up Davila probe by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Codelco hopes to wrap up Davila probe by year-end.

text.p: Chilean state copper company Codelco hopes to end its three-year probe into failed futures deals by ex-operator Juan Pablo Davila and bring any fresh charges by the end of the year, said a top Codelco official.
"We want to finish this (the investigation) by the end of the year, maybe by January," said senior sales vice president Juan Eduardo Herrera.
"We want to put this behind us as soon as possible. This is the third year and that's enough," he added.
Davila, a once high-flying copper trader, has been indicted by Chilean courts after his failed deals cost Codelco, the world's largest copper producer, $175 million in 1993.
Codelco is considering bringing legal charges against at least one more company, in addition to the two law suits it has started against brokers in London, Herrera told reporters.

"We haven't taken the final decision as we don't have all the information yet," he said. "If we find a strong case against any company, we will press charges...We are analyzing more than one situation."

Although he was cleared this year by Chilean courts of a conviction for tax evasion, the former trader still faces charges of tax fraud and "carrying out business incompatible" with his position in Codelco.
Davila, fired as soon as the losses were uncovered in early 1994, was freed on bail recently from preventative detention in a Santiago jail after undergoing cancer surgery.
